long_biography.plain_text:
Ferrovial began as the railway-construction company Rafael del Pino Moreno founded in Madrid. His son, Rafael del Pino Calvo-Sotelo, trained as a civil engineer and later became chief executive. During his management, the group acquired Agroman, entered North American concessions with Toronto's 407 ETR and completed its public listing.

After becoming chairman in 2000, del Pino oversaw an acquisition-led expansion that brought Poland's Budimex, Britain's Amey and the BAA airports group into Ferrovial. The company evolved from a Spanish builder into an international transport-infrastructure investor and operator, with toll roads and airports central to its portfolio. Del Pino now controls roughly 22% of Ferrovial through Rijn Capital, combining an inherited family stake with more than three decades of active executive stewardship.
long_biography.html:
Ferrovial began as the railway-construction company Rafael del Pino Moreno founded in Madrid. His son, Rafael del Pino Calvo-Sotelo, trained as a civil engineer and later became chief executive. During his management, the group acquired Agroman, entered North American concessions with Toronto's 407 ETR and completed its public listing.

After becoming chairman in 2000, del Pino oversaw an acquisition-led expansion that brought Poland's Budimex, Britain's Amey and the BAA airports group into Ferrovial. The company evolved from a Spanish builder into an international transport-infrastructure investor and operator, with toll roads and airports central to its portfolio. Del Pino now controls roughly 22% of Ferrovial through Rijn Capital, combining an inherited family stake with more than three decades of active executive stewardship.
